name: Centro and the Flower Clock
tagline: The grid between the estuary and the beach, with the casino
description: Vina's commercial core laid out on a grid of numbered streets between the Marga Marga estuary and the sea, with the casino, the shopping streets, the flower clock and the Quinta Vergara park at its southern edge. It is flat, walkable and where most services sit.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the beach, the shops and the metro within a short walk
pros: Flat and genuinely walkable, beach included
Metro to Valparaiso and Limache from the centre
Quinta Vergara park and the festival amphitheatre
cons: Rents at the top of the local market
Busy and noisy in the Chilean summer
Street crime has risen and requires attention

name: Renaca
tagline: The beach suburb north, towers above the sand
description: The coastal district north of Vina, built as apartment towers stepping up the hillside above a long beach, with restaurants along the front and a summer crowd that fills it entirely in January and February. It is the most sought-after beach address on this coast.
bestFor: Stays that want a modern flat with the beach directly below
pros: Long sand beach and the promenade at the door
Restaurants and beach bars along the front
cons: The highest rents on the coast, especially in summer
Extremely crowded in January and February

name: Recreo and the Valparaiso Boundary
tagline: Between the two cities, hillside streets and lower rents
description: The residential slopes at the southern end of Vina where it runs into Valparaiso, with older apartment buildings on the hillside, sea views and rents noticeably below the centre. The metro runs along the shore below, putting both city centres within ten minutes.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting sea views at a lower rent, with both cities close
pros: Rents below both Vina centre and Renaca
Metro to both city centres in ten minutes
cons: Steep streets and long stair climbs
Requires more caution than central Vina

name: Agua Santa and Forestal
tagline: The wooded ravines inland, quiet and residential
description: The residential districts climbing the ravines inland from the centre, greener and considerably quieter, with houses and low blocks under eucalyptus and a settled year-round population. Rents are well below the coast and the centre is ten minutes down the hill.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting quiet, trees and rents below the beachfront
pros: Green, quiet and away from the summer crowds
Rents well below the coastal districts
Ten minutes down to the centre

name: Valparaiso Cerro Alegre and Concepcion (10 km south)
tagline: The painted hills of the UNESCO port next door
description: The two hills above Valparaiso's port that hold the city's restored quarter, reached by the surviving funicular lifts, with painted houses, street art, small hotels and the best restaurant and bar scene on this coast. It is ten minutes from Vina by metro.
bestFor: Stays that want Valparaiso's character rather than Vina's beaches
pros: The best bar, restaurant and arts scene in the region
UNESCO-listed hills, funiculars and street art
Ten minutes by metro to Vina
cons: Street crime is a genuine concern on the hills
